title: Best Dehumidifier Brands (2026): 8 Top Makers Ranked
dek: The logo on the front matters less than who built the machine and how long they’ll stand behind it. Here’s how eight big names really stack up.
description: The best dehumidifier brands of 2026, ranked by warranty, who builds them and reliability — plus whether budget names like Pelonis and Waykar are any good.
intro: Shop for a dehumidifier and you’ll see a dozen brand names on the shelf — so which dehumidifier brands are actually good? Start with what you won’t see on the box: several of them roll off the same production lines. A surprising share of the room units sold in the U.S. are built by **Midea**, whether the badge says Midea, GE, hOmeLabs or something else entirely, so two “competing” machines can be close cousins under the plastic.

That’s why this guide ranks companies rather than individual models. A brand tells you two things a spec sheet won’t: who actually engineered the hardware, and how long the warranty protects you if the compressor gives out in year three. We compared eight brands on warranty terms, manufacturing source, lineup breadth, recall history and published reliability survey data.
If you already know your brand and want a specific model, jump to our [best dehumidifier](/best/best-dehumidifier/) roundup. If you’re still deciding whose name you trust, start here.
topPicksLead: For most single-room buyers, **Midea** is the brand to beat: it has the broadest lineup of room dehumidifiers here and earns a top predicted-reliability score in Consumer Reports’ member survey.

products.name: Midea — Cube 20-Pint Smart Dehumidifier (MAD20S1QWT)
pros: Broadest capacity ladder, from Cube 20 to Cube 50 with pump
Top predicted-reliability score in Consumer Reports’ survey
Cube 20 carries ENERGY STAR Most Efficient status
Same core hardware sold under several other badges
cons: Standard warranty is just one year
Two-year coverage only on select retailer models
products.whyWeLoveIt: Midea wins on range and reliability together. Whether you need a small bedroom unit or a 50-pint machine with a built-in pump, there’s a Cube that fits, and the brand sits in the small group of names that Consumer Reports members rate highest for predicted reliability.
products.performance: In Consumer Reports’ brand-reliability survey, Midea is one of the few brands to earn a top score — ahead of brands that charge more for so-called premium hardware. The trade-off is coverage: a one-year standard warranty is well short of what Frigidaire and Honeywell offer. Our [best Midea dehumidifier](/best/best-midea-dehumidifier/) guide breaks down each Cube size.

products.name: Frigidaire — 50-Pint Wi-Fi Dehumidifier (FHDD5034W1)
pros: Five-year warranty on the sealed refrigeration system
Sold almost everywhere, online and in stores
Lineup spans a 22-pint budget unit to a smart 50-pint
products.whyWeLoveIt: Frigidaire is the safe, familiar default. It’s been in the category for decades, you can buy it at practically any big-box store, and its sealed-system warranty runs four years longer than what Midea, GE and LG offer.
products.performance: The lineup brackets the needs of most homes, from the compact FFAD2233W1 for a bedroom to the Wi-Fi and Alexa-enabled FHDD5034W1 for a basement. It doesn’t lead on app polish or model count, but it’s a dependable pick if you’d rather buy from a store you already know. See every model in our [best Frigidaire dehumidifier](/best/best-frigidaire-dehumidifier/) roundup.

products.name: GE — 50-Pint Dehumidifier with Built-In Pump (APYR50LC)
pros: SmartHQ app for remote humidity checks and full-tank alerts
APYR50LC named Best Overall by RTINGS in March 2026
Built-in pump on the flagship 50-pint model
cons: Built by Midea under license, so little hardware difference
products.whyWeLoveIt: GE’s strength is the everyday experience. The SmartHQ app is among the more polished in the category, and pairing it with a built-in pump means you rarely have to touch the machine once it’s set up.
products.performance: The APYR50LC earned an independent Best Overall nod from RTINGS’ March 2026 round, which speaks to its day-to-day usability. Underneath, GE’s dehumidifiers are Midea-built under license, so you’re largely paying for the software and the badge. Our [best GE dehumidifier](/best/best-ge-dehumidifier/) guide compares the full lineup.

products.name: hOmeLabs — 50-Pint Wi-Fi Dehumidifier (HME031003N)
pros: Midea-built hardware for less money
Wi-Fi and voice control on the 50-pint model
Strong value per pint
cons: No ENERGY STAR Most Efficient models in the current lineup
products.whyWeLoveIt: hOmeLabs is the easiest way to get Midea engineering at a lower price. If the logo matters less to you than the bottom line, it’s a sensible place to start.
products.performance: The HME031003N is a 50-pint (DOE) unit with Wi-Fi and voice control that typically undercuts similarly equipped Midea, GE and Frigidaire models. None of the current lineup reaches ENERGY STAR’s Most Efficient tier, so a Cube 20 will cost less to run in a small room. Pelonis is another Midea-built budget badge worth cross-shopping — see our [best Pelonis dehumidifier](/best/best-pelonis-dehumidifier/) guide.

products.name: LG — 50-Pint Dehumidifier with Pump (UD501KOJ5)
pros: One 50-pint size, three feature levels — easy to choose
Pump and Wi-Fi versions available
PuriCare ThinQ model for smart-home users
cons: One-year standard warranty and premium pricing
products.whyWeLoveIt: LG removes the sizing puzzle. Every current model is a 50-pint unit, so the only real decision is whether you want a pump and Wi-Fi — a refreshingly short shopping list.
products.performance: The range runs from the no-pump UD501KOG5 to the pump-equipped UD501KOJ5 and the ThinQ-connected PuriCare Sonoran DT501BKR0. If your space genuinely needs 50 pints, that simplicity is a plus; if you need a 20-pint bedroom unit or a 70-pint basement machine, LG simply doesn’t sell one. More in our [best LG dehumidifier](/best/best-lg-dehumidifier/) guide.

products.whyWeLoveIt: If warranty length is your tiebreaker, Honeywell is the portable brand to beat. You get a year of parts and labor plus four more years on the compressor, evaporator, condenser and refrigerant tubing.
products.performance: Consumer Reports has rated the TPFIT50AWK among the stronger large-capacity models it rated. Honeywell doesn’t build these machines itself: JMATEK has engineered and manufactured them under license since 2014. The one recurring complaint in owner reviews is what happens after year five, when repairs can be slow and expensive. Compare it head-to-head in [Frigidaire vs. Honeywell](/compare/frigidaire-vs-honeywell-dehumidifier/).

products.name: Aprilaire — E070 Crawl Space Dehumidifier

Ties into ductwork or sits out of sight

products.whyWeLoveIt: Aprilaire is for people sizing an entire basement or crawl space, not a bedroom. Every model drains continuously, so there’s no tank to empty no matter how much water it pulls.
products.performance: The range starts with the 70-pint E070 for crawl spaces and climbs to the 130-pint E130. The E100 earns ENERGY STAR’s Most Efficient designation; the E070 is the only model in the family without it. Expect a four-figure price before installation. See our [best Aprilaire dehumidifier](/best/best-aprilaire-dehumidifier/) guide for model-by-model detail.

products.name: Santa Fe — Ultra V100 Ventilating Dehumidifier

Ultra V100 adds fresh-air ventilation and MERV-13 filtration

products.whyWeLoveIt: No other brand here backs its hardware for as long. For a machine that may run thousands of hours a year in a basement, six years of coverage is real peace of mind.
products.performance: The Ultra V100 is rated at 100 pints a day for spaces up to about 2,300 square feet, and it brings in outside air through an integrated 8-inch duct while filtering to MERV-13 — an air-quality bonus Aprilaire’s line doesn’t emphasize. The Advance2 undercuts Aprilaire’s E070 for crawl-space jobs. More in our [best Santa Fe dehumidifier](/best/best-santa-fe-dehumidifier/) guide.

blocks.text: That reliability survey drew on 11,944 members who bought 13,632 dehumidifiers between 2014 and 2025. The most common failures were excessive noise and dead compressors or pumps — exactly the parts a longer sealed-system warranty covers.

sections.heading: How we pick the best dehumidifier brands

blocks.text: We don’t run a test lab. Instead, we compare what each brand publishes and what independent sources report: capacity under the 2019 DOE test procedure, ENERGY STAR certification records (which also name the actual manufacturer), warranty documents, owner’s manuals and CPSC recall notices.

We weighted warranty length and manufacturing source most heavily, then lineup breadth, smart features and reliability survey results. Finally, we read owner reviews for patterns — failed pumps, noisy compressors, slow service — and noted any brand whose name appears in a recall.

sections.heading: What to look for in a dehumidifier brand

items.label: A sealed-system warranty
items.text: The compressor is the expensive part. A brand that covers it for five years is betting its hardware will last.

items.label: Who really builds it
items.text: ENERGY STAR listings name the certifying manufacturer. If two brands share a factory, buy on price, warranty and features rather than the logo.

items.label: A lineup that fits your space
items.text: Some brands skip small or large capacities entirely. Check our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) before committing to a brand.

items.label: A clean recall record
items.text: Search the CPSC site for the exact model number, especially when buying used or on clearance.

items.label: Efficiency credentials
items.text: ENERGY STAR — and especially the Most Efficient tier — matters for a machine that may run all summer.

blocks.text: Licensing is common in appliances: one company owns the brand name, another builds the product. In dehumidifiers, that web is especially tangled.

items: **Midea’s family:** Midea builds its own Cube line plus GE-branded units under license, hOmeLabs, Pelonis, Keystone and Toshiba, according to ENERGY STAR certification records.
**Honeywell:** made by JMATEK, which added dehumidifiers to its Honeywell-licensed lineup in 2014 — not by Honeywell International and not by Midea.
**Haier and GE:** Haier has owned GE Appliances since 2016, yet GE’s dehumidifiers come from Midea. See [Haier vs. GE](/compare/haier-vs-ge-dehumidifier/) for the side-by-side.
**TCL and De’Longhi:** the two share a joint-venture factory in Zhongshan, China, so units under both logos can come from the same floor.

blocks.title: Check for the 2021 recall
blocks.text: A 2021 CPSC recall of dehumidifiers made by New Widetech covered specific older models sold under several names, including Haier, Friedrich, Ivation, De’Longhi and Amana. Some current model names closely resemble recalled ones, so confirm the full model number before buying secondhand.

sections.heading: Are budget brands like Pelonis and Waykar any good?

blocks.text: For dehumidifiers, yes — with caveats. Pelonis is better known for heaters and fans, but ENERGY STAR lists GD Midea as the manufacturer of every certified Pelonis dehumidifier, and its 50-pint pump model carries essentially the same rating as Midea’s own equivalent. The catches are small buckets and efficiency ratings that sit right on the certification floor. Our [best Pelonis dehumidifier](/best/best-pelonis-dehumidifier/) guide matches each model to its Midea twin.
Is Waykar a good dehumidifier brand?

Several Waykar models are genuinely efficient — a few meet ENERGY STAR’s Most Efficient criteria — but the model names are misleading. Waykar measures capacity at 95°F and 90% humidity, so an “80-pint” unit is rated about 25 pints a day under the DOE test. Buy on the DOE figure, not the name. Our [best Waykar dehumidifier](/best/best-waykar-dehumidifier/) guide decodes the lineup.

sections.heading: Which dehumidifier brand should you buy?

items: **One room, most people:** Midea, for its lineup and reliability score.
**Longest portable coverage:** Honeywell or Frigidaire, each with five years on the sealed system.
**Lowest price:** hOmeLabs, which sells Midea-built hardware for less.
**Best app:** GE and its SmartHQ platform.
**Least decision fatigue:** LG, with one capacity and three feature levels.

**Whole basement or crawl space:** Aprilaire for the widest capacity range, Santa Fe for the longest warranty and built-in ventilation. Our [best crawl space dehumidifier](/best/best-crawl-space-dehumidifier/) guide goes deeper.

blocks.text: In practice, the bigger decision is the category: a portable room unit usually lands in the $200–$450 range and plugs in, while a ducted whole-home system runs $1,400 and up and is installed like HVAC equipment.

**Midea** is the best dehumidifier brand for most people thanks to its range of sizes and top-tier reliability score, though its one-year warranty is short. If coverage matters more, choose **Honeywell** or **Frigidaire** for a portable unit, or **Santa Fe** for a whole-home system. And remember that several badges share Midea hardware — so when two models look alike, let warranty, efficiency and price decide.

faqs.q: What is the best dehumidifier brand overall?
faqs.a: Midea, for most buyers. It sells the widest range of room dehumidifiers among the brands here and earns a top predicted-reliability score in Consumer Reports’ member survey. Its weak spot is a one-year standard warranty.

faqs.q: Which dehumidifier brand has the longest warranty?
faqs.a: Santa Fe, at six years on units built since January 2024. Among portable brands, Honeywell offers five years total (one year parts and labor plus four on the sealed system), and Frigidaire covers its sealed system for five years. Midea, GE and LG default to one year.

faqs.q: Are some dehumidifier brands made by the same company?
faqs.a: Yes. Midea builds its own units plus GE-branded models under license, hOmeLabs and several other budget badges. Honeywell dehumidifiers are a separate case — they’re built by JMATEK under license.

faqs.q: Is Pelonis a good dehumidifier brand?
faqs.a: Generally, yes. Pelonis dehumidifiers are built by Midea, according to ENERGY STAR’s certification records, and perform like their Midea counterparts. Expect small buckets and basic efficiency, and buy from an authorized seller so the warranty applies.

faqs.q: Is Waykar a good dehumidifier brand?
faqs.a: Its better models are efficient and well priced, and some meet ENERGY STAR’s Most Efficient tier. Just ignore the pint number in the model name — it’s measured in hot, humid conditions and runs roughly three times the DOE rating.

faqs.q: Which dehumidifier brand is most reliable?
faqs.a: In Consumer Reports’ latest brand-reliability survey, Midea, Keystone, Toshiba and Perfect Aire earned the top predicted-reliability score. Across all brands, about 19% of units were likely to have a problem within four years.

faqs.q: Should I buy a portable or a whole-home dehumidifier brand?
faqs.a: Choose a portable brand like Midea, Frigidaire or Honeywell for a single room or a modest basement. Move to Aprilaire or Santa Fe when you need to dry an entire basement or crawl space, want continuous bucketless drainage, or prefer a unit tied into ductwork. See our [best whole-house dehumidifier](/best/best-whole-house-dehumidifier/) guide.
